rule: A visual producer binds this exact registry before generation and clears every applicable negative. Positive exemplars teach bounded patterns; they do not authorize reuse, publication or a surface style by themselves.

patterns: faceted light and anatomically informed linework
positiveExemplars.limits: Style authority for episode people only. It is not another character's identity, a location reference, a scene brief or site-building style approval.
Approved for its named identity job only. It is not a generic narration-matched scene, character-motion reference or permission to reuse episode-specific symbols.

negativeExemplars.prevention: Bind the destination style authority and every character identity reference; compare the rendered subject at face and full-body scale.
Bind the exact town/location authority and reject invented geography, people, props or scene roles.
Specify object surfaces, supports, orientations and connections before generation; inspect the real pixels for impossible devices such as a laptop screen on the outside lid.
Specify required bodies and actions before generation; inspect every visible hand, limb, finger, joint and body connection in the real pixels.
Default to clean art with deterministic editable text. If lettering is itself the asset, bind approved copy and compare every character in the rendered output.
Bind scene year, location, character age, wardrobe, accessories, technology and prohibited anachronisms before generation; inspect the rendered pixels.
Bind the exact accompanying words, time window, proposition and visual job. A shared mood or topic is not semantic alignment.
Give every dominant object, person, gesture and overlay a named scene or teaching job; remove anything that distracts, contradicts or merely decorates.
Describe the semantic event or justified ambient action; camera drift, a pan or a zoom cannot substitute for required change.
Classify loop, transition or one-shot before animation. Loops prove zero net travel; directional motion is never repeated as a loop.
Review the decoded final occurrence with its exact narration clock, crop, overlays and assembly transforms—not only the source clip.
